To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
BLCL can be generated without FCS, and that they are as effective as BLCLS for reactivating EBV‐specific CD4‐ and CD8‐CTL.
EBV‐specific CTL can be generated in vitro with BLCL0, and that these BLCL0 cells are as effective as BLCSF in stimulating the EBV‐reactive repertoire of the corresponding blood donor.

EBV‐transformed BLCL can be generated in serum‐free conditions and are as effective as their FCS‐containing counterparts in stimulating the EBV‐reactive T‐cell repertoire of the corresponding donors in vitro.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the generation of serum‐free BLCL and their use in the selection of EBV‐specific cytotoxic T lymphocyte.
the development of an EBV‐BLCL‐based assay that is free of any risk of infection, immunological or otherwise, and which is applicable to clinical settings.
the generation of BLCL in the absence of fetal calf serum.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

BLCL can be created in serum‐deprived media and that they retain their antigen‐presented capacities, but that the use of FCS‐containing medium may be preferable for the generation of BLCL for use in the clinical setting.
BLCL0 can be used for the generation of EBV‐specific CTL, as they are as effective as BLCLS in reactivating EBV‐specific CD8+ and CD4+‐T‐lymphocytes.
serum can be omitted in BLCL selection, and that this may be of particular interest for the generation of BLCL for clinical application.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
BLCL0 cells can be used as a tool for the generation of EBV‐specific cytotoxic T lymphocyte (CTL).
the BLCL0 cells can be used to stimulate EBV‐specific CTLs in vitro.
BLCL can be generated in the absence of FCS, and that these cells are as efficient as their FCS‐supplemented counterparts in stimulating the EBV‐reactive T‐cell repertoire.
The main takeaway from our work is that
serum‐free BLCL can be used as a substrate for the selection of EBV‐specific CTL.
BLCL0 can be used as an alternative to BLCLFCS for the selection of EBV‐specific CTL, and for the generation of EBV‐CTL‐based vaccines.
serum‐free BLCL are a valid option for the selection of EBV‐specific CTL for clinical applications.
